industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, and energy led the week; energy is the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior at industry level. Not Double Overweight at the industry because the industry holds Metals and mining (relative strength F now from A) and Agriculture beside the three energy sectors; Downstream distribution carries the A. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, two months into leadership is where reversals begin, and 13 of the 18 upstream Pool names read F on TSR/Valuation, so the market has paid.

sector.key: P.3. Energy - services and engineering contractors
sector.why: Overweight, carried and better supported. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Kepler Cheuvreux (29 October) separates services from producers: Subsea7's vessels are booked for 18 to 24 months with a pipeline above $20 billion and replacement vessels costing $750 to 800 million, so pricing holds regardless of spot crude; GTT's sell-off is 'overdone' with 550 to 650 LNG carriers over ten years; Aker Solutions guides 2027 earnings above consensus (Danske Bank, 28 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: C now, C prior, the market has not paid yet. Seven Pool names (SBM Offshore first on the starting score, Tenaris eighth, Odfjell Drilling, Saipem, Subsea 7). Not A because this is the most operationally geared, smallest-company end of energy and the Fragility axis punishes that; counter-case: Sell-side Momentum is D on Subsea 7 and Saipem. To A if relative strength leaves C with Sell-side Momentum turning up across the names; back to C if Brent falls under $85.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Spain this week (a source pack is present, 2026-W43, and it carried nothing country-specific here), relative strength is not graded by country, and Richard's view is G10 and Europe-wide with no country line. An absence is an absence; no tilt.
